memories.title: Fridge Oracle
memories.tools: Optical flow, segmentation, tracking, deblurring, OCR, stereo depth, a ranking model
memories.text: A computer vision pipeline that turns a short video of a fridge or pantry into a dated inventory and a cooking plan. It picks usable keyframes, segments and tracks each item so nothing is counted twice, reads the printed expiration dates with OCR, and estimates how much of each item is left. Recipes are then ranked by how much soon-to-expire food they use up, and anything past its date is flagged.
list: Keyframes (Modules 3 + 6): optical flow drops redundant frames from the sweep; a Fourier-domain sharpness score rejects motion-blurred ones
Items (Modules 4 + 6): classical segmentation separates each item from the shelf, checked against SAM2; Lucas-Kanade tracking links the same item across frames
Dates (Module 3 + OCR): date stamps are located, deconvolved to undo blur, read with OCR, and parsed across formats like “BEST BY 12/04” and “EXP 04DEC26”
Quantity (Modules 2 + 7): a known-size reference sets metric scale, and stereo depth finds items hidden behind others and estimates fill levels
Planning: items get an urgency score from days left, and recipes are ranked by how much urgent food they use while needing the fewest extra purchases
